appellations.name: Gries
appellations.summary: Gries is the old garden suburb of Bolzano on the alluvial fan of the Talfer river, and the historic home of Lagrein. The deep, warm gravel and sand soils, sheltered by the Guncina hill and baked by the hottest summers of the region, give dark, velvety Lagrein with violet and cocoa notes. The Benedictines of Muri-Gries have made wine here since the nineteenth century, and Cantina Bolzano's Lagrein Riserva Taber is a benchmark.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial gravel and sand of the Talfer delta on the flat valley floor; Bolzano's basin traps heat, so this is one of Italy's warmest red-wine sites north of the Alps. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 240 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
appellations.nerd_note: 'Lagrein Gries' was a recognised traditional name long before the UGA system; the 2024 UGA turns it into a defined site.
appellations.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

appellations.terroir: Alluvial gravel and sand at the foot of the porphyry slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 240 to 410 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Lagrein.
appellations.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
